title: Pricing, contracts and growing a tutoring business
audience: Tutors and education coaches (draft shell, no teaching content yet)
learningOutcomes: Set a session price and a package price that cover the tutor's preparation, travel, reporting and administration as well as teaching time, and show the client what each price includes.
Write cancellation, late-arrival and make-up terms, and get the client to accept them in writing before the first session.
Describe what an invoice must show, and set out a referral arrangement that the business can record and check.

instruction.heading: Working out a session price
instruction.body: A session price must cover more than the time spent with the learner. Add the time for preparation, marking, writing progress notes, travel and administration to the teaching time. For example, a tutor who teaches for one hour, prepares for thirty minutes and writes notes for fifteen minutes is working for one hour and forty-five minutes for that session, and the price should reflect that. Compare the rate with local rates taken from a published source, and record the source and the date checked. Do not set a price by copying a competitor's advertised rate without checking what that rate includes.

instruction.heading: Cancellation and make-up terms
instruction.body: Write down the notice needed to cancel or move a session, what counts as a late cancellation or a no-show, whether a make-up session is offered, and how payment is treated in each case. The client should accept these terms in writing before the first session, and the accepted version should be kept with the client record. Whether these terms fit consumer law in the state or territory is UNCONFIRMED in this lesson and must be checked before the terms are used.

instruction.heading: Invoices and payment records
instruction.body: Each invoice should show the business name and contact details, the client's name, the date, the service provided, the number of sessions, the rate, any amount due, and the payment terms. Whether the invoice must also carry a registration or tax number, or be issued as a tax invoice, depends on the tax registration of the business and is UNCONFIRMED here. Check it with the business's accountant or the official tax source. Record each payment against the invoice it pays, and keep the record for the period the business rules set.

instruction.heading: Referrals
instruction.body: Ask for a referral only from a client who has been satisfied with the service, and record where each new client came from. Do not offer a payment, discount or gift for a referral until the wording, the cost and any tax treatment have been confirmed. Do not make promises about a learner's results in any marketing, including referral messages. Describe what the service does and what it includes.
